title: FAA Part 107 operating rules practice questions
description: Free FAA Part 107 operating rules practice questions on 14 CFR 107 Subparts A and B. Every answer is explained and linked to its section.

questions.topic: Applicability and definitions
questions.question: How does 107.3 define a control station?

options.A: An interface used by the remote pilot to control the flight path of the small unmanned aircraft
options.B: A ground facility from which air traffic control issues airspace authorizations
options.C: The place where the visual observer must stand during the flight
options.D: Any vehicle from which a small unmanned aircraft is launched

questions.explanation: 107.3: "Control station means an interface used by the remote pilot to control the flight path of the small unmanned aircraft."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.3, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Control station means an interface used by the remote pilot to control the flight path of the small unmanned aircraft.

questions.topic: Applicability and definitions
questions.question: Which of these does 107.1(b) list as an operation to which Part 107 does not apply?

options.A: Any commercial photography operation
options.B: Air carrier operations
options.C: Any flight at night
options.D: Any flight in Class G airspace

questions.explanation: 107.1(b) states that "This part does not apply to the following" and lists first "Air carrier operations".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.1, Applicability (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (1) Air carrier operations;

questions.topic: Applicability and definitions
questions.question: How does 107.3 define a visual observer?

options.A: Any person who watches the flight from the ground
options.B: A person who holds a remote pilot certificate and controls a second aircraft
options.C: A person designated by the remote pilot in command to assist the remote pilot in command and the person manipulating the flight controls to see and avoid other air traffic or objects aloft or on the ground
options.D: An FAA inspector who observes the operation to check compliance

questions.explanation: 107.3: a visual observer is "a person who is designated by the remote pilot in command to assist the remote pilot in command and the person manipulating the flight controls of the small UAS to see and avoid other air traffic or objects aloft or on the ground."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.3, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Visual observer means a person who is designated by the remote pilot in command to assist the remote pilot in command and the person manipulating the flight controls of the small UAS to see and avoid other air traffic or objects aloft or on the ground.

questions.topic: Remote pilot in command and crew
questions.question: When does 107.19(a) require a remote pilot in command to be designated?

options.A: Only after the flight, when the flight is logged
options.B: Only when the flight takes place in controlled airspace
options.C: Only when a visual observer is used
options.D: Before or during the flight of the small unmanned aircraft

questions.explanation: 107.19(a): "A remote pilot in command must be designated before or during the flight of the small unmanned aircraft."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.19, Remote pilot in command (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: A remote pilot in command must be designated before or during the flight of the small unmanned aircraft.

questions.topic: Remote pilot in command and crew
questions.question: What does 107.19(c) require the remote pilot in command to ensure in the event of a loss of control of the small unmanned aircraft for any reason?

options.A: That the small unmanned aircraft will pose no undue hazard to other people, other aircraft, or other property
options.B: That the small unmanned aircraft is insured against damage to itself
options.C: That air traffic control is told about the loss of control before the next flight
options.D: That the visual observer takes over the flight controls

questions.explanation: 107.19(c): the remote pilot in command "must ensure that the small unmanned aircraft will pose no undue hazard to other people, other aircraft, or other property in the event of a loss of control of the small unmanned aircraft for any reason."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.19, Remote pilot in command (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The remote pilot in command must ensure that the small unmanned aircraft will pose no undue hazard to other people, other aircraft, or other property in the event of a loss of control of the small unmanned aircraft for any reason.

questions.topic: Remote pilot in command and crew
questions.question: Under 107.21(b), what must a remote pilot in command who deviated from a rule in an in-flight emergency do upon request of the Administrator?

options.A: Send a written report of that deviation to the Administrator
options.B: Surrender the remote pilot certificate for cancellation
options.C: Retake the initial aeronautical knowledge test
options.D: Apply for a certificate of waiver covering the deviation

questions.explanation: 107.21(b): each remote pilot in command who deviates from a rule under paragraph (a) "must, upon request of the Administrator, send a written report of that deviation to the Administrator."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.21, In-flight emergency (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Each remote pilot in command who deviates from a rule under paragraph (a) of this section must, upon request of the Administrator, send a written report of that deviation to the Administrator.

questions.topic: Remote pilot in command and crew
questions.question: Without a certificate of waiver, what does 107.35 say about operating more than one unmanned aircraft?

options.A: A remote pilot in command may operate up to three aircraft at once if each has a visual observer
options.B: A person may operate two aircraft at once if both are in Class G airspace
options.C: A person may not manipulate flight controls or act as a remote pilot in command or visual observer in the operation of more than one unmanned aircraft at the same time
options.D: Only the visual observer may watch more than one aircraft at the same time

questions.explanation: 107.35: "A person may not manipulate flight controls or act as a remote pilot in command or visual observer in the operation of more than one unmanned aircraft at the same time."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.35, Operation of multiple small unmanned aircraft (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: A person may not manipulate flight controls or act as a remote pilot in command or visual observer in the operation of more than one unmanned aircraft at the same time.

questions.topic: Remote pilot in command and crew
questions.question: Which regulations does 107.27 require a person manipulating the flight controls, the remote pilot in command and the visual observer to comply with on alcohol or drugs?

options.A: Part 120 only
options.C: 49 CFR Part 382
options.D: § 61.53 only

questions.explanation: 107.27 requires these persons to "comply with the provisions of §§ 91.17 and 91.19 of this chapter."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.27, Alcohol or drugs (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: A person manipulating the flight controls of a small unmanned aircraft system or acting as a remote pilot in command or visual observer must comply with the provisions of §§ 91.17 and 91.19 of this chapter.

questions.topic: Preflight and condition for safe operation
questions.question: If the small unmanned aircraft is powered, what does 107.49(d) require the remote pilot in command to ensure prior to flight?

options.A: That the battery is less than one year old
options.B: That a spare battery is on site
options.C: That there is enough available power for the small unmanned aircraft system to operate for the intended operational time
options.D: That the power source is listed on the Certificate of Aircraft Registration

questions.explanation: 107.49(d): "If the small unmanned aircraft is powered, ensure that there is enough available power for the small unmanned aircraft system to operate for the intended operational time".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.49, Preflight familiarization, inspection, and actions for aircraft operation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: If the small unmanned aircraft is powered, ensure that there is enough available power for the small unmanned aircraft system to operate for the intended operational time;

questions.topic: Preflight and condition for safe operation
questions.question: Which item does 107.49(a) list as part of the operating environment assessment the remote pilot in command must make prior to flight?

options.A: The aircraft's resale value
options.B: The pilot's flight hours in the last 90 days
options.C: The manufacturer's warranty status
options.D: Local airspace and any flight restrictions

questions.explanation: The 107.49(a) assessment "must include" "Local weather conditions", "Local airspace and any flight restrictions", "The location of persons and property on the surface" and "Other ground hazards."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.49, Preflight familiarization, inspection, and actions for aircraft operation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (2) Local airspace and any flight restrictions;

questions.topic: Reporting, inspection and waivers
questions.question: Which of these does 107.9(a) list as a criterion that makes an operation reportable to the FAA?

options.A: Damage to the small unmanned aircraft itself
options.B: Serious injury to any person or any loss of consciousness
options.C: Any loss of the control link, with no injury or damage
options.D: Any flight that ends with a landing away from the launch point

questions.explanation: 107.9(a) covers an operation involving at least "Serious injury to any person or any loss of consciousness"; 107.9(b) covers damage to property "other than the small unmanned aircraft".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.9, Safety event reporting (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Serious injury to any person or any loss of consciousness

questions.topic: Visual line of sight and visual observers
questions.question: Which purpose does 107.31(a) list for being able to see the unmanned aircraft throughout the entire flight?

options.A: To record video for the person who hired the flight
options.B: To determine the unmanned aircraft's attitude, altitude, and direction of flight
options.C: To read the registration number marked on the aircraft
options.D: To confirm that the Remote ID broadcast is working

questions.explanation: 107.31(a) requires seeing the unmanned aircraft throughout the entire flight in order to, among other things, "Determine the unmanned aircraft's attitude, altitude, and direction of flight".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.31, Visual line of sight aircraft operation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Determine the unmanned aircraft’s attitude, altitude, and direction of flight;

questions.topic: Visual line of sight and visual observers
questions.question: If a visual observer is used, what does 107.33(a) require of the remote pilot in command, the person manipulating the flight controls and the visual observer?

options.A: They must all hold remote pilot certificates
options.B: They must stand within 10 feet of each other
options.C: They must maintain effective communication with each other at all times
options.D: They must log the flight with ATC

questions.explanation: 107.33(a): they "must maintain effective communication with each other at all times."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.33, Visual observer (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The remote pilot in command, the person manipulating the flight controls of the small unmanned aircraft system, and the visual observer must maintain effective communication with each other at all times.

questions.topic: Night and civil twilight
questions.question: What does 107.29(d) say about night operations under a certificate of waiver issued prior to April 21, 2021 under 107.200?

options.A: After May 17, 2021, no person may operate a small unmanned aircraft system at night in accordance with such a waiver
options.B: Such a waiver stays valid for night operations with no end date
options.C: Such a waiver allows night operations without anti-collision lighting
options.D: Such a waiver must be renewed every 24 calendar months

questions.explanation: 107.29(d): "After May 17, 2021, no person may operate a small unmanned aircraft system at night in accordance with a certificate of waiver issued prior to April 21, 2021 under § 107.200."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.29, Operation at night (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: After May 17, 2021, no person may operate a small unmanned aircraft system at night in accordance with a certificate of waiver issued prior to April 21, 2021 under § 107.200.

questions.topic: Night and civil twilight
questions.question: How does 107.29(c)(3) define civil twilight in Alaska?

options.A: From 30 minutes before official sunrise until 30 minutes after official sunset
options.B: The same 30-minute periods that apply in the rest of the United States
options.C: The hours of darkness listed in the Chart Supplement U.S.
options.D: The period of civil twilight as defined in the Air Almanac

questions.explanation: 107.29(c)(3): "In Alaska, the period of civil twilight as defined in the Air Almanac." The 30-minute periods in (c)(1) and (c)(2) apply "Except for Alaska".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.29, Operation at night (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: In Alaska, the period of civil twilight as defined in the Air Almanac.

questions.topic: Hazardous operations and right of way
questions.question: Without a certificate of waiver, what does 107.25(a) say about operating a small unmanned aircraft system from a moving aircraft?

options.A: It is allowed over a sparsely populated area
options.B: It is allowed when the moving aircraft flies below 400 feet AGL
options.C: It is allowed when a visual observer rides in the moving aircraft
options.D: No person may operate a small unmanned aircraft system from a moving aircraft

questions.explanation: 107.25: "No person may operate a small unmanned aircraft system" "From a moving aircraft". The sparsely populated area exception in 107.25(b) applies only to "a moving land or water-borne vehicle".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.25, Operation from a moving vehicle or aircraft (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: No person may operate a small unmanned aircraft system— (a) From a moving aircraft; or

questions.topic: Hazardous operations and right of way
questions.question: What does 107.37(b) prohibit?

options.A: Operating within 5 statute miles of any manned aircraft
options.B: Operating in any airspace class where manned aircraft fly
options.C: Operating a small unmanned aircraft so close to another aircraft as to create a collision hazard
options.D: Operating at a groundspeed higher than that of a nearby manned aircraft

questions.explanation: 107.37(b): "No person may operate a small unmanned aircraft so close to another aircraft as to create a collision hazard."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.37, Operation near aircraft; right-of-way rules (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: No person may operate a small unmanned aircraft so close to another aircraft as to create a collision hazard.

questions.topic: Airspace and operating limitations
questions.question: Unless otherwise authorized by the Administrator, what does 107.52 prohibit?

options.A: Operating a small unmanned aircraft system with its Remote ID broadcast on
options.B: Operating a small unmanned aircraft system under Part 107 with a transponder on
options.C: Operating a small unmanned aircraft system with its anti-collision lighting on during the day
options.D: Operating a small unmanned aircraft system while listening to the CTAF

questions.explanation: 107.52: "Unless otherwise authorized by the Administrator, no person may operate a small unmanned aircraft system under this part with a transponder on."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.52, ATC transponder equipment prohibition (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Unless otherwise authorized by the Administrator, no person may operate a small unmanned aircraft system under this part with a transponder on.

questions.topic: Airspace and operating limitations
questions.question: Which persons does the opening sentence of 107.51 require to comply with all of its operating limitations?

options.A: A remote pilot in command and the person manipulating the flight controls of the small unmanned aircraft system
options.B: Only the registered owner of the small unmanned aircraft
options.C: Only the visual observer, if one is used
options.D: Only the air traffic controller who authorized the flight

questions.explanation: 107.51: "A remote pilot in command and the person manipulating the flight controls of the small unmanned aircraft system must comply with all of the following operating limitations".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.51, Operating limitations for small unmanned aircraft (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Airspace and operating limitations
questions.question: How does 107.51(c) define flight visibility?

options.A: The distance at which the aircraft's anti-collision lighting can be seen
options.B: The vertical distance between the small unmanned aircraft and the cloud base
options.C: The distance a pilot can see down the runway in a moving aircraft
options.D: The average slant distance from the control station at which prominent unlighted objects may be seen and identified by day and prominent lighted objects may be seen and identified by night

questions.explanation: 107.51(c): "flight visibility means the average slant distance from the control station at which prominent unlighted objects may be seen and identified by day and prominent lighted objects may be seen and identified by night."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.51, Operating limitations for small unmanned aircraft (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: For purposes of this section, flight visibility means the average slant distance from the control station at which prominent unlighted objects may be seen and identified by day and prominent lighted objects may be seen and identified by night.
